dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real-valued function X on a measure space, this is its Bochner/Lebesgue integral ∫ X dμ as a real number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the numerator of the first upper bound, so that bound is μ({ω | X(ω) ≥ t}).toReal ≤ (∫ X dμ)/t.

dependency_coverage.name: And

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: The extended nonnegative real numbers, implemented as nonnegative reals with an added top element ∞.

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal.instPartialOrder

dependency_coverage.name: ENNReal.ofReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps a real number r to the extended nonnegative real corresponding to max(r,0).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It converts X pointwise and t into nonnegative extended reals for the lower-integral bound; since t>0, ENNReal.ofReal t represents t without truncation, while negative exceptional values of X are sent to zero.

binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is an arbitrary measure on Ω.
X:Ω→ℝ is an arbitrary real-valued function.
t∈ℝ is an arbitrary threshold, introduced after the assumptions on X and μ.
hypotheses: X is measurable from Ω to ℝ with its Borel measurable structure.
X is integrable with respect to μ.
The threshold is strictly positive: t>0.
conclusions: The real conversion of the measure of the upper-level event is bounded by the real integral divided by t: (μ({ω | X(ω)≥t})).toReal ≤ (∫ω, X(ω) ∂μ)/t.
The ENNReal measure of the same event is bounded by the lower integral divided by the ENNReal form of t: μ({ω | X(ω)≥t}) ≤ (∫⁻ω, ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) ∂μ)/ENNReal.ofReal(t).
mathematical_definitions: The first numerator is the real-valued Bochner/Lebesgue integral ∫ X dμ.
The second numerator is the ENNReal-valued lower integral ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(X) dμ.
For a real r, ENNReal.ofReal(r) is the extended nonnegative real corresponding to max(r,0).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measure space and every measurable, integrable real-valued function that is nonnegative almost everywhere, each positive threshold t satisfies both forms of Markov's inequality for the event where X is at least t: its real-valued measure is at most the integral of X divided by t, and its extended-nonnegative-real measure is at most the lower integral of the nonnegative embedding of X divided by the nonnegative embedding of t.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The threshold must satisfy t>0; the proposition says nothing for t≤0 and avoids division by zero.

Nonnegativity is required only μ-almost everywhere, not at every point. Consequently ENNReal.ofReal truncates any negative exceptional values to zero, while null-set changes do not affect the integrals or event measure.
The event uses X≥t, not X>t, because Set.Ici is the closed interval [t,∞).
No assumption that μ is a probability measure or finite measure is made.

The first conclusion uses ENNReal.toReal through Measure.real. Since conversion of an infinite ENNReal value does not preserve ∞ as a real number, that formulation alone can obscure or trivialize infinite-measure cases; the second ENNReal inequality retains infinity and is the stronger untruncated formulation. Under the stated integrability and positive-threshold hypotheses, the conclusion itself controls the threshold-event measure.

The statement assumes both pointwise measurability of X and Integrable X μ, even though integrability already contains an almost-everywhere strong measurability condition; these are distinct formal hypotheses.

The proposition asserts the two inequalities as a conjunction but does not explicitly assert that the real integral equals the lower integral after conversion, nor that the two displayed right-hand sides are equal.
If no function satisfies the three hypotheses for a chosen Ω and μ, the implication over such an X is vacuous; otherwise the conclusion applies to every positive t.
